policy: Accept the OpenAI theorem as true. Tasks seek improvements, not a baseline proof audit. Check live overlap; listing is not reservation or evidence of novelty.

tasks.question: Can realizable mode structure improve the root M/sqrt(u) enumeration cost?
tasks.first_step: Write the exact generating function for one changed mode family. Identify a constraint absent from the unrestricted weighted-partition envelope, then derive its complete asymptotic count.
tasks.success: A proved smaller exponent for a realizable mode family, with the new deformation/precision and child contracts stated. A scoped family result is useful even before global composition.
tasks.stop: Only a constant, finite histogram, or smaller upper bound with unachievable simultaneous parameters; record that scope before extending.
open_obligations: Complete recursive cost and all outer overheads

tasks.question: Can a changed packing, taper, or recursive schedule improve the logarithmic saving of the full contraction theorem?
tasks.first_step: Choose one changed schedule and write its root cost, depth-wise u and wire sizes, precision increments, entry cost and leaf threshold together. Compare its dominant exponent with the accepted model.
tasks.success: A simultaneously feasible full budget with a better contraction envelope, or a precise obstruction to the proposed schedule.
tasks.stop: Changing only the geometric recursion ratio or improving a term that another unchanged term dominates.
open_obligations: Packing, precision, entries, leaves and descriptions under that schedule

tasks.question: Can arbitrary-density sparse queries use fewer than O(n log log n) wires without paying the gain in entries or preprocessing?
tasks.first_step: Change one monomial-indexing or grouping choice. Charge index bits, invalid codes, group degree, tensor-entry work, number of arrays and all query/reduction branches.
tasks.success: A full improved general-density bound. Removing log log n is valuable but leaves alpha at 1/2; label it that way.
tasks.stop: Assuming fixed clause density, omitting rejected greedy query candidates, or hiding exponential entry work in a succinct tensor description.
open_obligations: All query instances, including candidates not selected by the greedy procedure

tasks.question: Can decision avoid exact-counting requirements and beat the accepted alpha or its logarithmic correction?
tasks.first_step: State the weaker interface being used and construct one candidate algorithm with an explicit per-input success probability and worst-run time bound. Name every place where exact counts were previously used.
tasks.success: A complete decision reduction or scoped new primitive with a quantified error and a paid total budget; space tradeoffs are allowed if explicit.
tasks.stop: An average-case input guarantee, expected-time-only guarantee, or a randomized polynomial identity step with unbounded or uncharged error amplification.
open_obligations: Correctness probability for each fixed input
Worst-outcome time and all amplification costs

tasks.question: Does a proposed change improve the complete exponent after all overheads are composed?
tasks.first_step: Copy the appropriate cost model into a new research package, add every changed and unchanged overhead, and run python3 -m satbounds.cost on it. Then attach a proof of the new assumptions or identify the missing one.
tasks.success: An exact cost comparison for a named proposal, with sufficient realizability conditions and remaining obligations. A cost-only screen remains conditional.
tasks.stop: Relabelling a hypothetical input exponent as an achieved algorithm, removing only iterated logs and claiming larger alpha, or comparing unspecified big-O constants numerically.
open_obligations: Proof that its inputs and parameter conditions can hold simultaneously
